newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Amplats signs access deal with rebel union.
newsitem.headline: Amplats signs access deal with rebel union.

text.p: Anglo American Platinum Corp Ltd (Amplats) said it had signed an agreement on Friday with the Mouth Peace Workers' Union granting it access rights to its mines, under certain conditions, for the purpose of recruiting members.

"Once representation has been verified in terms of the company's recognition criteria, the necessary recognition agreement will be negotiated," the world's largest platinum producer said in a statement.

Earlier in July two National Union of Mineworkers (NUM) officials and four of their family members were killed, continuing a wave of violence that first wracked Amplats' three platinum mines last May.
Its Rusplats mine has been plagued by a long-running dispute over union representation. It was hit in late May by a two-day wildcat strike.
A previous peace accord was signed on July 1 between labour unions at the mines aimed, but this was shatterd by the killings earlier this month.
Speculation in the local press has blamed the violence on conflict between the NUM and the Mouthpiece Workers' Union.
In May members of the Mouthpiece Workers' Union tortured two NUM members after a "kangaroo court" (informal trial). Some of those involved in the torture were dismissed.
In June two senior NUM leaders were killed by unknown gangs at the Amandelbult and Union sections of Rusplats.
Amplats produces about 1.8 million ounes of platinum a year.
Amplats' mines, including Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd and Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd, are situated in the Northern and North West provinces.
